Interval in milliseconds at which the Issuer is asked about the status of credential requests that are still awaiting their credentials. Each run is delayed by up to a fifth of it at random, so that runtimes do not poll in lockstep. Configuring a number <= 0 disables polling, and with it the timeouts of requests awaiting their credentials.
Time in milliseconds a credential request waits for its credentials before the Issuer is first asked about its status, as most Issuers deliver them within that time
Maximum time in milliseconds between two status queries for the same credential request. A request is asked about less often the longer it waits for its credentials, up to this interval.
The scope that will be used to issue an access token to be included in the Self-Issued ID token in the 'token' claim. By default, no token will be generated.
Time in seconds after which a credential request is considered failed if its credentials have not arrived, and its status cannot be queried, because the Issuer did not report its issuance process ID
Time in seconds after which a credential request is considered failed if its credentials have not arrived, although the Issuer keeps reporting it as pending
The iteration wait time in milliseconds in the state machine.
The number of entities to be processed on every iteration. They are leased together, so the lease must outlast the processing of all of them.

How long the entities of a batch are leased, in milliseconds. It must be longer than the processing of a whole batch, i.e. longer than the batch size times the call timeout, otherwise another runtime may process the same entities.
How many times a failed operation is retried before it fails with an error. With the default delays, the retries take about six hours.
The base delay of retries in milliseconds. The n-th retry waits the base delay times 2 to the power of n, but at most the maximum delay.
The maximum delay between two retries in milliseconds.
How long it may take to connect to the counterparty when a message is sent, in milliseconds.
How long it may take to send a message and receive the response, in milliseconds. A message that times out is not retried right away, but by the state machine, like any other failure.
How long a Verifiable Presentation is valid after it was created, in seconds. Determines the 'exp' claim of JWT presentations and the proof 'expires' of Linked-Data presentations.

Returns VCDM 2.0 presentations as the VP JWT itself, as defined by VC-JOSE-COSE, instead of wrapping it in an 'EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation' that is signed again as a JWT. Only enable this if all verifiers accept plain VP JWTs.

Verifies access tokens with keys from the vault or 'edc.iam.publickeys' if the participant context has no matching key pair. That lookup is not scoped to the participant context, so this should only be enabled for keys that are not managed as key pairs.
Rejects delivered credentials in formats whose proof cannot be verified, such as credentials with an embedded Linked-Data proof. If disabled, they are stored with a warning.

Whether requests to an Issuer's IssuerService endpoint, which is taken from the Issuer's DID document, must use HTTPS and may only be sent to hosts that resolve to public addresses, and whether redirects are not followed. Should be enabled if participants or Issuers are not trusted to only publish endpoints of legitimate Issuers in their DID documents.

Comma-separated list of hosts (host names or IP addresses) that requests to an Issuer's IssuerService endpoint may be sent to, although they use plain HTTP or resolve to loopback, link-local or private addresses, e.g. an Issuer running in the same cluster. Only has an effect if 'edc.iam.issuer.endpoint.restrict' is enabled.
